entries.author: observer
entries.text: Dana has managed permits and punch lists for dozens of kitchen renovations.

entries.author: observer
entries.text: Dana believes the rock-bottom bid is a trap that will inevitably lead to change orders or substandard materials.

entries.author: observer
entries.text: Dana holds that permits are non-negotiable for kitchen remodels to protect insurance coverage and resale value.

entries.author: observer
entries.text: Dana is confident that DIY electrical work poses severe fire and liability risks that outweigh any cost savings.

entries.author: observer
entries.text: Dana recommends a 10-15% initial deposit with subsequent payments tied to specific project milestones.

entries.author: observer
entries.text: Dana believes contractors who refuse milestone-based payment schedules are planning to exploit the homeowner financially.

entries.author: observer
entries.text: Dana is convinced that splitting permits between trades will cause inspection failures and project delays.

entries.author: observer
entries.text: Dana advises verifying workers’ compensation and insurance by contacting state licensing boards directly rather than trusting provided documents.

entries.author: observer
entries.text: Dana views the cheap contractor’s aggressive upfront payment demand as a major red flag warranting immediate contract revisions or termination.

entries.author: observer
entries.text: Dana is certain that even minor electrical modifications like outlet relocation legally trigger permit requirements in most jurisdictions.
